metadata.title: Magidor-like forcing and the cofinality of the Galvin number

nodes.name: The Galvin number
nodes.statement: Let gp be the minimal kappa such that every family C = {C_alpha : alpha in kappa^+} of clubs of aleph_1 contains a subfamily D = {C_{alpha_i} : i in omega_1} so that the intersection of D belongs to the club filter D_{aleph_1}.

nodes.name: The full Galvin number
nodes.statement: Let fgp be the first lambda for which every family C = {C_alpha : alpha in lambda^+} of clubs of aleph_1 contains a subfamily D of size lambda^+ such that the intersection of D belongs to the club filter D_{aleph_1}.

nodes.name: Galvin property Gal(F, partial, lambda)
nodes.statement: Given aleph_0 < kappa <= partial <= lambda and a normal filter F over kappa, Gal(F, partial, lambda) denotes the statement that every C subset of F of size lambda admits a subfamily D of size partial such that the intersection of D belongs to F.

nodes.name: The forcing M_{gamma,kappa}
nodes.statement: Let kappa be regular and uncountable with omega <= gamma < kappa. A condition p in M_{gamma,kappa} is a pair (s^p, A^p) with s^p in [kappa]^{<gamma}, A^p in [kappa]^kappa, and sup(s^p) < min(A^p). The ordering p <= q requires s^p subset s^q, angle-bracket inclusion on the measure-one parts, and that s^q - s^p = {}_omega t for some t in [A]^{<gamma}.

nodes.name: Weak partition cardinal
nodes.statement: A cardinal kappa is a weak partition cardinal if kappa -> (kappa)^gamma for every gamma in kappa.

nodes.name: Polarized partition relation
nodes.statement: The notation binom(alpha, beta) -> binom(gamma, delta) denotes the statement that for every coloring c: alpha x beta -> {0,1} one can find A in [alpha]^gamma, B in [beta]^delta so that c restricted to A x B is constant.

nodes.name: Ultimate failure of the Galvin property
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: Suppose C = {C_alpha : alpha in lambda} subset of D_{aleph_1} witnesses the failure of the Galvin property. We say C witnesses the ultimate failure of the Galvin property if lambda = 2^{omega_1}.

nodes.name: Claim 1.1 (Galvin property from measurability)
nodes.statement: If aleph_0 < kappa < lambda and both kappa and lambda are measurable, then Gal(U, lambda, lambda) holds whenever U is a normal ultrafilter over kappa.
assumptions: Both kappa and lambda are measurable cardinals
U is a normal ultrafilter over kappa
conclusions: The polarized relation binom(lambda, kappa) -> binom(W, U) holds for any normal ultrafilter W over lambda

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1.1
nodes.statement: First establishes the polarized relation binom(lambda, kappa) -> binom(W, U) by using lambda-completeness of W and normality of U to find monochromatic sets. Then derives the Galvin property by defining a coloring from the family of filter sets and applying the polarized relation.

nodes.name: Proposition 1.3 (Consistency strength of cf(fgp)=omega in ZFC)
nodes.statement: In ZFC, the statement cf(fgp) = omega has some consistency strength.
conclusions: The statement cf(fgp) = omega requires the failure of square^*_mu for every singular mu of countable cofinality below the continuum, which has consistency strength

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1.3
nodes.statement: Step 1: Shows that if mu is singular of countable cofinality with a scale (f_alpha) such that for every A in [mu^+]^{aleph_1} the set {f_alpha(n) : alpha in A, n in omega} has size aleph_1, then fgp != mu. Step 2: Shows that a good scale satisfies this property. If square^*_mu holds at every singular mu of countable cofinality below the continuum, then fgp != mu for all such mu, hence cf(fgp) > omega.

nodes.name: Claim 1.5 (Preservation of measurability of aleph_1)
nodes.statement: Let V be a model of AD and let G be V-generic for M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}. Then aleph_1 is measurable in V[G] and D_{aleph_1} is an ultrafilter.
assumptions: V is a model of AD
G is V-generic for M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}
conclusions: D_{aleph_1} is a normal ultrafilter over aleph_1 in V[G]

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1.5
nodes.statement: Under AD, aleph_1 is measurable (Solovay) and aleph_2 is a weak partition cardinal (Kleinberg). Hence M_{aleph_1, aleph_2} adds no subsets of aleph_1, so D_{aleph_1} remains a normal ultrafilter.

nodes.name: Main Claim 2.1 (Preservation of regularity of aleph_{omega+1})
nodes.statement: Assume AD and let G be V-generic for M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}. Then aleph_{omega+1} is regular in V[G].
assumptions: V is a model of AD
G is V-generic for M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}

nodes.name: Proof of Main Claim 2.1
nodes.proof_strategy: contradiction using partition relations and coloring argument
nodes.statement: Assumes toward contradiction that aleph_{omega+1} becomes singular in V[G]. Defines ordinals eta_{s,alpha} for stems s and ordinals alpha. Uses the partition relation aleph_2 -> (aleph_2)^{<omega_1} to find a monochromatic set q. Shows that the range of the cofinal function is bounded, yielding a contradiction.

nodes.name: Claim 2.2 (Cofinality and polarized relations)
nodes.statement: Three related statements: (a) If kappa = cf(lambda) then binom(lambda, kappa) does not arrow binom(lambda, kappa). (b) If Gal(D_kappa, lambda, lambda) holds then binom(lambda, kappa) -> binom(lambda, kappa). (c) If kappa = cf(lambda) then not Gal(D_kappa, lambda, lambda).
conclusions: (a): binom(lambda, kappa) does not arrow binom(lambda, kappa)

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2.2
nodes.statement: Part (a): Constructs a coloring using the cofinality sequence, showing no monochromatic product of full size exists. Part (b): Given a coloring, uses the Galvin property to find monochromatic sets. Part (c): Follows from (a) and (b) by contraposition.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.3 (Main theorem: fgp = aleph_omega)
nodes.statement: One can force over a model of AD to obtain fgp = aleph_omega, and hence cf(fgp) = omega.
assumptions: V is a model of AD with V = L(R)
conclusions: There exists a generic extension V[G] (by M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}) which is a model of ZF where fgp = aleph_omega

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.3
nodes.proof_strategy: forcing with Magidor-like forcing over AD model
nodes.statement: Forces with M_{aleph_1, aleph_2} over V = L(R) model of AD. Uses Claim 1.5 to preserve measurability of aleph_1. Uses Main Claim 2.1 to preserve regularity of aleph_{omega+1}. Shows fgp <= aleph_omega: since no new subsets of aleph_1 are added, any aleph_{omega+1}-sequence of clubs has at most aleph_1 distinct elements, giving the Galvin property. Shows fgp >= aleph_omega: for each finite n, cf(aleph_n) = omega_1 in V[G] (since cf(aleph_n) = omega_2 under AD), so Claim 2.2(c) gives failure of Gal(D_{aleph_1}, aleph_{n+1}, aleph_{n+1}).

nodes.name: Question 2.4 (Measurability of aleph_{omega+1} in generic extension)
nodes.statement: Let V be a model of AD, and let G be V-generic for M_{aleph_1, aleph_2}. Is aleph_{omega+1} a measurable cardinal in V[G]? Is the collection of omega-closed unbounded subsets of aleph_{omega+1} a normal ultrafilter in V[G]?

nodes.name: Claim 3.1 (gp with cofinality omega_1 in ZFC)
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: Assume GCH. One can force gp = lambda whenever lambda > cf(lambda) = omega_1. Moreover, this statement has no consistency strength.
conclusions: The statement cf(gp) = omega_1 has no consistency strength

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.1
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: Uses the Abraham-Shelah forcing to add lambda-many Cohen reals and clubs witnessing failure of Galvin property. Since cf(lambda) = omega_1, one gets 2^omega = lambda < 2^{omega_1}, and hence Gal(D_{aleph_1}, aleph_1, lambda^+) holds by a result from the literature, giving gp = lambda.

nodes.name: Remark 3.3 (Cardinal arithmetic from cf(gp) = omega)
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: If mu > cf(mu) = omega and gp = mu, then 2^theta = mu^+ for every aleph_0 <= theta <= mu.
conclusions: 2^theta = mu^+ for every aleph_0 <= theta <= mu

nodes.name: Proof of Remark 3.3
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: If 2^mu > mu^+ then there is a good scale at mu^+, contradicting gp = mu. If 2^{aleph_0} < mu then gp <= 2^{aleph_0} < mu. Hence 2^{aleph_0} >= mu^+, and since 2^{aleph_0} <= 2^mu = mu^+, all power sets in the range equal mu^+.

nodes.name: Question 3.2 (Alouf's question)
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement: Is it consistent that mu > cf(mu) = omega_1, gp = mu, and yet every family D in [D_{aleph_1}]^mu satisfies the Galvin property?
